Here the limits of the numerator and denominator are ${lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}=\infty $ and ${lim}_{x\to 0}(\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}-1)=\infty ,$ respectively, so we have the case $\frac{\infty }{\infty }.$

Applying L'Hopital's rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}-1)} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{[\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}]}^{′}}{{[\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}-1]}^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{(-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}})}{(-\frac{4}{{x}^{5}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{2{x}^{-3}}{4{x}^{-5}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{x}^{2}}{2} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
